record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometric Methods for Instance-Based Learning
record.original_question: For the k-nearest-neighbor decision rule, how fast does the probability of error Pe[k-NN] converge to the Bayes error Pe as the training-set size n tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: How fast does the error rate Pe[k-NN] approach the Bayes error Pe as n approaches infinity, and what is the finite-sample performance of the k-NN-rule

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,Y)$ be a random pair taking values in $\mathbb{R}^d \times \{1,2,\dots,M\}$ with joint distribution $P$, where $X$ is the feature vector and $Y$ is the class label. Given an i.i.d. training sample $\mathcal{D}_n = \{(X_1,Y_1),\dots,(X_n,Y_n)\}$ drawn from $P$, and an integer $k \ge 1$, the $k$-nearest-neighbor (k-NN) decision rule classifies a query point $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ by majority vote among the labels $Y_{(1)}(x),\dots,Y_{(k)}(x)$ of the $k$ training points whose features $X_i$ are closest to $x$ under the Euclidean metric (ties broken in a fixed way). Let
$$P_e[\text{k-NN}](n) \;=\; \Pr\!\big(g_{n,k}(X) \neq Y\big)$$
denote the probability of error of the k-NN rule (where $g_{n,k}$ is the classifier built from $\mathcal{D}_n$), and let
$$P_e^* \;=\; \inf_{g} \Pr(g(X) \neq Y)$$
denote the Bayes error (the infimum over all measurable classifiers $g:\mathbb{R}^d \to \{1,\dots,M\}$).

(a) Determine the rate at which $P_e[\text{k-NN}](n) - P_e^*$ tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$ (with $k=k(n)$ chosen suitably, e.g.\ $k(n)\to\infty$ and $k(n)/n \to 0$), in terms of natural assumptions on the underlying distribution $P$ (smoothness/Lipschitz conditions on the regression function $\eta(x) = \Pr(Y=1\mid X=x)$, margin conditions, and dimension $d$).

(b) Provide non-asymptotic (finite-sample) bounds on $P_e[\text{k-NN}](n) - P_e^*$ as a function of $n$, $k$, and the distributional parameters.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on this classical question. Under margin (Tsybakov-type) and smoothness assumptions on the regression function, both asymptotic rates such as $O(k^{-(1+\alpha)/2}) + O((k/n)^{(\alpha+1)/d})$ and finite-sample/minimax-optimal bounds (e.g.\ $O(n^{-4/(d+4)})$ with local choice of $k$) have been established by Chaudhuri–Dasgupta, Samworth, Gadat–Klein–Marteau, Döring–Györfi–Walk and others. General consistency ($P_e[\text{k-NN}]\to P_e^*$ when $k\to\infty,\ k/n\to 0$) is classical (Stone, 1977). Sharp rates without distributional assumptions or under minimal assumptions remain an active research area, so the question is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Rates of convergence for nearest neighbor classification (Chaudhuri–Dasgupta)
status_evidence.snippet: Finite-sample misclassification rate bounded by an 'effective boundary' term, no distributional assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Finite-sample rates for k-NN exist under general conditions.

status_evidence.title: Rate of Convergence of k-Nearest-Neighbor Classification Rule (JMLR)
status_evidence.snippet: E{L(gn,k)} − L* = O(1/k^{(1+α)/2}) + O((k/n)^{(α+1)/d}) under weak margin and Lipschitz conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Tight upper bounds on excess risk are known under margin and smoothness.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic expansions of the k-nearest-neighbor risk (Annals of Statistics)
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic expansions of k-NN risk as n→∞.
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotic expansions of the excess risk have been derived.
